  Deputy Knott presented the Sheriff Department report for the month of August 2022

  Assistant Fire Chief Drew Smith presented the Fire Department report for the month
  of August 2022 including the number of fires, medical response calls, and rescue

  are back in action for fire season.

  (https://www.conejochamber.org/).

l

  Councilmember Davis moved to adopt Resolution No. 2270-22, approving

  conjunction with a restaurant at 30869 Thousand Oaks Boulevard, Ox Bone Ramen.

  3.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT NO. 22-002:
  RESOLUTION NO. 2272-22

  Senior Planner Sinkula presented Planned Development Permit (PDP) No. 22-002,
  authorizing the construction of a new 2,696 square foot, two-story, single-family
  residence with an attached 398 square foot, two-car garage located at 4008
  Whitesail Circle, in the Westlake Island Neighborhood, along with a request for a
  demolition permit, after the fact, for the prior 2,513 square foot home at 4008
  Whitesail Circle.

  On June 8, 2022, the Planning Department received notification from the Westlake
  Island Homeowners Association (HOA) that a single-family residence was
  demolished at 4008 Whitesail Circle without approval from the HOA, the City, or Los
  Angeles County Building and Safety. Staff notified Los Angeles County Building and
  Safety and a stop work order was issued at the site on June 9, 2022.

 j  Staff then began working with the property owner, Carol Melville, and on June 22,
  2022, and an application to apply for the required Planned Development Permit to
  authorize the construction of a new residence was submitted. The application was
  determined to be complete on August 9, 2022.

  The subject lot is 5,236 square feet and is located within the Westlake Island
  neighborhood and the Residential Planned Development (RPD-153) Zone. The
  applicant is requesting authorization for the demolition of an existing 2,513 square
  foot, two-story (20 feet 3 inches tall) single-family residence with an attached 398

  square foot, two-car garage, after the fact, and the construction of a new 2,696
  square foot, two-story (25 feet 10 inches tall) single-family residence with an
  attached 398 square foot two-car garage.

  Senior Planner Sinkula explained that the proposed design is compatible with the
  mix of architectural styles on Westlake Island and the Westlake Island HOA has
  approved the proposed project. The applicant conducted outreach to all neighbors
  who expressed support for the design of the new residence. The residence, as
  proposed, conforms to the applicable height and lot coverage requirements for the
  residential zone, meets the required front, rear, and side yard setbacks, and

  On September 15, 2022, the permit request was reviewed by the Land Use

  the full City Council for hearing pending confirmation that the project had the support
  of the neighbors of the project site.

  Applicant Carol Melville addressed City Council.

  Councilmember Davis moved to adopt Resolution No. 2272-22, approving Planned

  foot two-story single-family residence with an attached 398 square foot two-car

MONTHLY IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

1.  Engineering Department Report

  City Engineer Hughes stated the COG has obtained $15 million in Measure R funds
  available this fiscal year. In August, COG approved Westlake Village's $1.3 million
  sidewalk projects, all three sidewalk segments on Lindero Canyon Road, to receive
  Measure R funds. Measure R projects will be presented to the Los Angeles County
  Metropontan Transportation Authority in January 2023 for consideration/approval. If
  approved, in February 2023, the City will be allowed to move forward with the
  sidewalk project with possible completion within the fiscal year.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  September 28, 2022  7

  MONTHLY IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS (continued):

l
  2.  Planning Department Report

  Planning Director Forbes provided an update on the status of the City's comment
  letter for Pure Water Project Environmental Impact Report (EIR) proposed by the
  Las Virgenes-Triunfo Joint Powers Authority (JPA). The comment letter will address
  impacts to Westlake Village related to construction (noise, air quality, traffic) and
  operational impacts (aesthetics, biological, recreation) with constructing the
  Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) at alternative site 1 in Agoura Hills.

  Alternative site 2, located near the Westlake Village reservoir, would result in
  additional environmental impacts with the construction of a vehicle access road,
  laying additional water pipelines and electrical lines, while impacting recreational,
  biological, and aesthetic impacts due to trail closure, tree removals, and habitat
  disruption. Therefore, the City is supporting AWPF site 1, in Agoura Hills, as the
  environmentally superior location.

  Staff will submit the comment letter by the October 7th deadline and review the JPA
  comments and final EIR once published.

  3.  Cultural Recreation Report

  Community Services Specialist Roush provided details on the City Celebration event
  to be held October 15, 2022 from 3:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m., at City Hall, noting the 20th
  anniversary. Holidays in the Village will be held on December 4, 2022. This year's
  event will include the City's annual Holiday Sing-Along as part of the Holiday's in the
  Village European Marketplace hosted by the Westlake Village Rotary and will be
  held at the County Line Shopping Center off Lakeview Canyon Road and Agoura
  Road.

  Deputy City Manager Eskandar thanked Community Services Specialist Roush for
  her efforts in planning the City's special events.

j  Councilmember Davis moved to approve the Consent Calendar. Councilmember Honig

OLD BUSINESS:

1.  PRESENTATION OF ASSET MANAGEMENT PLAN

  City Manager de Geus reported this is the final report on the Reserve Study and
  Asset Management Plan (AMP). Mr. de Geus provided an overview of the project,
  stating that City Council approved a contract with Kayuga Solutions, Inc., staff
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  September 28. 2022  9

  OLD BUSINESS (continued):

l
  worked with Kayuga, with project results presented to the Environmental Committee,
  the City conducted a Study Session on this topic, and the project is now being
  finalized.

  Mr. de Geus reported that Kayuga used the asset data to create an Infrastructure
  Reinvestment Intelligence Systems (IRIS) database and trained city staff on
  maintaining the database, allowing the City to understand current needs, forecast
  future maintenance, capital investment needs, and build reserves to maintain our
  infrastructure. City Engineer Hughes and Public Works Manager Iverson were the
  key staff working on this project.

  Founder and President of Kayuga Solutions, Inc., Colin Chung, presented the
  project approach which identified critical assets, desired level of service, cost of
  ownership and expected lifetime. A total of 8, 106 assets, of which 89% are in good
  to excellent condition, were assigned to four categories: Building (1,183 assets),
  Parks and Parkways (2,069 assets), Roadway (4,476 assets), and Storm Drainage
  {378 assets) and inventoried into IRIS. IRIS maintains a historical log for each asset
  to assist with forecasting future funding needs, monitoring asset usage, and
  determining lifespan of the asset.

  City Council received and filed the Asset Management Study.

  NEW BUSINESS:

  1.  AWA.RD OF LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICE CONTRACTS TO
  AMERICAN HERITAGE LANDSCAPE AND BRIGHTVIEW LANDSCAPE
  SERVICES

  City Manager de Geus reported that the Landscape Request for Proposal (RFP) was
  an extensive process with interviews, Environmental Committee review, and
  American Green Zone Alliance (AGZA) review related to the City's Zero-Emission
  for Landscape Equipment initiative.

j
  City Engineer Hughes presented the Landscape Maintenance RFP, issued on July
  15, 2022, and designed to require vendors to transition to electric powered
  equipment in lieu of gas powered two-stroke engines. The RFP outlined the method
  by which city vendors would achieve AGZA certification each contract year. Ms.
  Hughes stated that achieving the Green Zone Level 1 Certification is key to
  addressing the stated City Council Goal for "sustainable Westlake Village" and the
  RFP was written to allow the City to award a single vendor or two vendors with
  separate contracts for the Community Park Streetscape and Park Maintenance.
  Four RFP responses were received with three applicants interviewed by staff. Staff
  is recommending that two contracts be awarded: Brightview maintaining Community
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  September 28, 2022  10

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  Park maintenance and janitorial services, and American Heritage Landscape
  maintaining the remaining streetscape and park maintenance for the City. Both
  vendors are professionally qualified, dedicated to proper staffing levels to meet the
  City's high standards of care, and also meet established sustainability goals of
  achieving the Green Zone Level 1 Certification.

  City Council discussion transpired concerning the selection of one versus two
  vendors and pricing models.

  Councilmember Honig moved to approve a contract with American Heritage, in the
  amount of $2,228,752 for the purpose of city-wide landscape maintenance services
  and a contract with Brightview, in the amount of $969,408 for landscape
  maintenance and janitorial services at the Community Park and authorize the Mayor
  to execute the contracts on behalf of the City. Mayor Pro Tern Pearl seconded the
  motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern
  Pearl, and Mayor Halpern
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN :  None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0.

  Councilmember Davis stated this action is a significant step towards achieving City
  Council's goal towards sustainability in Westlake Village and places Westlake
  Village in a leadership role in Conejo Valley.

2.  LANDSCAPE IRRIGATION CONTROLLER UPGRADE PROJECT - YEAR 3 -
  SITEONE LANDSCAPE SUPPLY, AMERICAN HERITAGE LANDSCAPE AND
  ARROYO IRRIGATION CONTRACT AWARDS

  City Engineer Hughes presented a recommendation to the Council for approval of
  an Irrigation Controller Purchase Agreement with SiteOne Landscape Supply
  (SiteOne) in the amount of $144,967.39, an Irrigation Flow Sensor Purchase
  Agreement with American Heritage Landscape (American Heritage) in the amount
  of $48,708 and a Professional Services Agreement with Arroyo Irrigation (Arroyo) in
  the amount of $46,475.75. She mentioned that the landscape controller project was
  presented to the Environmental Committee on September 13, 2022. Ms. Hughes
  explained that the project adjusts the City's irrigation system to receive water savings
  of up to 30% when fully deployed and noted that with two years deployed, 25% water
  reduction have been achieved. Originally a five-year project, in Fiscal Year 2022-
  2023, funding was increased to complete the project one year early.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  September 28, 2022  11

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  She added that HydroPoint controllers will continue to be utilized, adding 15
  controllers/sites this fiscal year. After contracts are approved, WaterSmart rebates
